name: Tower Bridge
hint: Nothing may stand in the river except the two towers. Hang the side spans from chains over the towers, and carry the middle from above - like the high-level walkways.

history.name: Tower Bridge
history.engineer: Sir Horace Jones (architect), Sir John Wolfe Barry (engineer)
history.span: Central span 61 m · side spans 82 m
facts: The two bascules of the central span lift so tall ships can reach the Pool of London; steam-driven hydraulics raised them until the 1970s.
On 30 December 1952 bus driver Albert Gunter accelerated his No. 78 bus across a widening gap as the bridge began to open - and landed safely.
The high-level walkways, 44 m above high water, tie the two towers together; they closed in 1910 and reopened as an exhibition in 1982.
history.why: London needed a low road and a tall ship channel at the same place. Tower Bridge solved it with a road that lifts between towers that also anchor suspension spans.
history.note: The game cannot lift a bascule: the tall ship channel is the no-build zone, and the walkways inspire the structure above the deck.
